selected_priority: Recover stranded live experience-graph intelligence from the estate-intelligence compiler lineage and compose it onto current main without reverting stronger later code.
displaced_capability: Current main retained a strong estate compiler but lacked the stranded live experience-graph runtime that dynamically connects owned repositories to company challenge mappings and personal paradigms, discovers previously unseen repository families, and emits privacy-separated public/internal graph projections with deterministic snapshot identity.

mechanisms_compared.assessment: Whole-branch restoration was rejected because feature/estate-intelligence-compiler-v2 was only 5 commits ahead but 275 commits behind current main. Restoring that snapshot would displace extensive later application, company-intelligence, recovery, and estate work.

Reimplementing the graph inside the modern estate_compiler module was credible but would duplicate a substantial historically proven runtime and increase regression risk without first recovering its distinct branch-owned semantics.

Selected: preserve current main intact while composing only the branch-owned experience graph runtime, policy, schema, adversarial tests, and focused proof surface forward from the exact historical lineage.

maps repositories independently to company challenges and personal engineering paradigms instead of collapsing those concepts
discovers previously unseen repository families from live inventory without requiring code changes
emits distinct internal and public graph projections
omits private repository identities from the public graph while retaining sanitized flagship presence

binds source digests and the complete graph state into a deterministic snapshot_id
writes graph artifacts atomically and fails closed on malformed source records
restores a machine-readable schema and an explicit policy surface for aliases, paradigms, family discovery, and privacy
